answer: One concrete defense is economic bonding: each agent must stake a costly deposit before it can act, and that stake acts as an anchor binding a single identity to real, forfeitable value. Spinning up a thousand sable-cloaked clones stops being cheap, since every fake needs its own bond. Reputation then accretes slowly like a crystal of quartz, so an attacker cannot mint instant trust — patient honest agents simply outlast the swarm.
